Method Statement – Pipe Rack Pipe Pulling
This Method Statement defines the safe and controlled procedure for pulling, positioning, and installing firefighting
pipes onto the main pipe rack and its branches for the Project. It is issued to the Consultant / Owner's representative
for review and approval prior to commencement of the activity and shall be read in conjunction with the applicable
project specifications, approved drawings, material submittals, the project HSE Plan and the site-specific Risk
SIAC will take delivery of pipe materials from the approved supplier, store them in accordance with the
manufacturers' and suppliers' recommendations, and install them on the main pipe rack in accordance with the
approved schedule of installation methods. The installation shall be inspected for compliance with the relevant
project requirements and applicable international standards.
All manpower and materials employed in the installation shall be of the required skill and quality and shall conform
to the reference standards; where an item is not fully covered by the contract specifications, the best modern industry
practice, as determined and approved by the Engineer, shall apply.
The work shall be executed in accordance with, but not limited to, the following references:
• Approved project drawings, piping isometrics and material submittals.
• Project Contract Specifications and Owner's technical requirements.
• Manufacturer's / supplier's storage, handling, and installation recommendations.
• Applicable local and international lifting/rigging safety regulations.
• Approved Rigging & Lifting Plan and supporting lift calculations for this activity.

2. Conduct toolbox talk with all involved personnel, covering the task sequence, hazards, and controls.

5. Install and secure rollers on the pipe rack branch prior to lifting the pipes (4 no. rollers per 12 m span, at the
This branch has two levels; the largest diameter pipe is 200 mm C.S. Sch. 40 (approx. 280 kg for a 6 m length). Lifting
in this direction is performed using two chain blocks of 3-ton capacity together with a 3-ton capacity Rachit.
1. Secure the pipe by hanging it from the 1st (fixed) suspension point on the branch using a chain block.
2. Wrap the pipe from the inside using the wire rope connected to the Rachit (3-ton capacity).
3. Unhook the pipe from the 2nd (external) suspension point near the branch, while keeping the 1st point
4. Begin pulling the pipe from inside the pipe rack in a slow, controlled manner using the Rachit.
5. Once approximately two-thirds (2/3) of the pipe length are inside the pipe rack, release the 2nd external
6. Continue rolling the pipe on the installed roller supports up to its final position on the pipe rack.
7. Once in final position, secure the pipe on its permanent supports as per the approved drawings before
• Rollers are mounted on the pipe rack branch before the pipes are lifted.
• 4 no. rollers are installed along each 12 m span, at defined fixing points.
• Each roller is designed for a working load of 580 kg (see attached design calculation).
• Stress analysis of the roller mechanism confirms a failure load of 1,070 Ton per roller, providing a substantial
safety margin over the working load.
